I tracked each variable by finding its last real (non-commented) direct assignment. Then I applied every later `+ k mod 100` update in order. All lines marked "stale log; do not execute" were ignored.

**a** — the last direct assignment is `a <- 72`. Fifty-three increments follow: 8, 92, 80, 74, 46, 54, 26, 28, 92, 68, 40, 60, 40, 46, 14, 86, 46, 8, 92, 54, 54, 92, 54, 14, 40, 46, 54, 60, 86, 54, 46, 14, 40, 92, 54, 14, 40, 92, 68, 86, 46, 8, 60, 40, 46, 46, 8, 46, 54, 60, 86, 14, 32. Applied one at a time mod 100, these bring a back to **72**.

**b** — the last direct assignment is `b <- 7`.
- The next ten increments (73, 72, 55, 19, 81, 45, 74, 26, 55, 19) take b to 26.
- The 53 increments after `a <- 72` total a multiple of 100, so b ends at **26**.

**c** — the last direct assignment is `c <- 80`.
- The ten increments before `b <- 7` take c to 26.
- The nine increments between `b <- 7` and `a <- 72` take it to 80.
- The 53 increments after that leave it at **80**.

**d** — the last direct assignment is `d <- 40`. The 44 increments that follow (32, 54, 46, 54, 54, 92, …, 8, 92, 68) total a multiple of 100, so d ends at **40**.

**TMP** — there is no real direct assignment after the initial `TMP <- 11`, so I applied every TMP increment in the program from the start.
- The first few steps give 11 → 2 → 2 → 52 → 8 → 36 → …
- At the point of `a <- 72`, TMP is 26.
- The remaining increments end at **80**.

ANSWER: a ?= 72; b ?= 26; c ?= 80; d ?= 40; TMP ?= 80;
